children: Denmark's central bank raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.10% on Thursday as expected, following the European Central Bank's decision earlier in the day to hike rates.

"The interest rate increase is a consequence of the increase by the European Central Bank of its main monetary policy rate, the deposit facility rate, by 0.25 percentage point. Thereby, the monetary policy spread vis-a-vis the euro area will remain unchanged," the central bank said in a statement.

The ECB on Thursday raised its interest rates for the second time this year to fight off an energy-driven inflation surge, as the war in the Middle East continues and global bond yields have risen sharply over the past week.
Denmark's Nationalbank's primary mandate is to keep the crown stable in a narrow trading band against the euro, an objective it upholds through currency interventions and interest rate moves.
The central bank intervened twice this year to defend the crown peg, as the crown has weakened slightly over the past years, to levels last seen in the first quarter of 2020, according to LSEG data.

Denmark's benchmark current account interest rate and the certificate of deposit rate were each raised by 25 basis points to 2.10% from 1.85%, while the so-called lending rate was raised by 25 basis points to 2.25% from 2.00%.
